Aditya / team — I ran a preliminary calculation and attached credit_calc.xlsx. Summary below:

- SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime.
- Billing period: Apr 1–30 (30 days = 720 hours).
- Customer-reported outage window: Apr 14 03:20–05:30 UTC ≈ 2.17 hours.
- Uptime impact fraction = 2.17 / 720 = 0.301% of the month.

Per our credit policy table (section 4.2 in SOW): for monthly uptime < 99.9% but >= 99.0% we apply a 10% credit of monthly recurring fees; for <99.0% a 25% credit. The impacted fraction corresponds to a monthly uptime of ~99.699% (720 - 2.17 = 717.83 hours up => 717.83/720 = 0.99701). That falls in the 99.0–99.9% bracket => 10% credit.

Customer’s monthly MRR for invoice INV-4321 = $28,400 (I pulled this from billing). 10% credit = $2,840.

Notes/next steps:
- This is our suggested credit amount. Credits above $5k require finance notification; above $10k require legal sign-off. At $2.84k we can approve internally.
- I attached the calc tab with timestamps and rounding.
- Recommend issuing a credit memo applied to the May invoice and sending a formal credit_statement.pdf to the customer for their records.

If everyone is good, I can prepare the credit memo and mark as applied to INV-4321 for the May billing run.

Marissa
Director, Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
